entry.title: Fe²⁺ homogeneous catalysis of I⁻ / S₂O₈²⁻
entry.observation: Fe²⁺ pale-green solution may become more yellow/brown as Fe³⁺ forms; colour change may be masked at low concentration
entry.notes: first catalytic step; Fe²⁺ is regenerated in the next step.

entry.title: Regeneration of Fe²⁺ in I⁻ / S₂O₈²⁻ catalysis
entry.observation: iodine gives a yellow-brown / brown solution; with starch gives blue-black
entry.notes: second catalytic step; catalyst is regenerated.

entry.title: NO / NO₂ homogeneous catalysis of SO₂ oxidation
entry.reagent: NO acts in a catalytic cycle
entry.observation: NO is colourless; NO₂ is brown gas

entry.title: NO₂ oxidises SO₂
entry.observation: brown NO₂ is consumed; NO formed is colourless
entry.notes: completes the atmospheric NOx catalytic cycle. ---

entry.title: Thermal decomposition of Group 2 nitrates
entry.observation: white CuI precipitate forms together with brown iodine solution
entry.notes: iodine may be confirmed with starch → blue-black. ---

entry.title: Benzene chlorination
entry.observation: chlorine colour is consumed; HCl may be evolved; no single distinctive observation is normally required

entry.title: Benzene bromination
entry.observation: bromine colour is consumed; no white precipitate
entry.notes: **do not confuse with phenol/phenylamine**, which react with Br₂(aq) without AlBr₃.

entry.title: Benzene nitration
entry.observation: no distinctive required colour change; nitrobenzene is a pale-yellow oily liquid in practice

entry.title: Methylbenzene side-chain halogenation
entry.temperature: light / mild heating may be used
entry.notes: conditions determine **side-chain** substitution; `AlCl₃/AlBr₃` instead promotes **ring** substitution. ---

entry.title: Formation of chlorobenzene / bromobenzene
entry.reagent: AlCl₃ for chlorination / AlBr₃ for bromination
entry.notes: same chemistry as A2-30-01/02; listed again because Topic 31 explicitly requires the preparation route.

entry.title: Alcohol acylation
entry.observation: reaction occurs readily; steamy/acidic HCl fumes may be seen
entry.notes: no concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst is required. ---

entry.title: Phenol + sodium metal
entry.observation: effervescence; sodium disappears; H₂ gives a squeaky pop

entry.title: Phenol bromination
entry.observation: bromine water decolourises and a **white precipitate** forms

entry.title: Carboxylic acid + PCl₃
entry.section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
entry.observation: corrosive reaction; no single standard CIE observation required

entry.title: Carboxylic acid + PCl₅
entry.section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
entry.observation: steamy/acidic HCl fumes may be observed

entry.title: Carboxylic acid + SOCl₂
entry.section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
entry.observation: gas evolution; steamy acidic HCl fumes; SO₂ also evolved
entry.notes: gaseous by-products help drive reaction forward. ---

entry.title: Methanoic acid + Tollens' reagent
entry.notes: methanoic acid is an exception among ordinary carboxylic acids.

entry.title: Methanoic acid + acidified KMnO₄
entry.observation: purple → colourless; CO₂ may be evolved

entry.title: Methanoic acid + acidified K₂Cr₂O₇
entry.observation: orange → green; CO₂ may be evolved

entry.title: Ethanedioic acid + warm acidified KMnO₄
entry.observation: purple solution decolourises; effervescence of CO₂
entry.notes: slow at first when cold; becomes faster as Mn²⁺ builds up. ---

entry.title: Acyl chloride hydrolysis
entry.observation: rapid/vigorous reaction; steamy acidic HCl fumes may be observed
entry.notes: much more readily hydrolysed than chloroalkanes or chlorobenzene.

entry.title: Acyl chloride + alcohol
entry.observation: reaction occurs readily; HCl fumes may be seen
entry.notes: ester formation; no concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst needed.

entry.title: Acyl chloride + phenol
entry.medium: non-aqueous / weakly basic trapping conditions may be used experimentally
entry.observation: ester forms; HCl may be evolved
entry.notes: e.g. benzoyl chloride + phenol → phenyl benzoate.

entry.title: Amide reduction with LiAlH₄
entry.notes: C=O group is reduced to CH₂.

entry.title: Nitrile reduction with LiAlH₄
entry.notes: carbon chain is retained; nitrile carbon becomes CH₂.

entry.title: Nitrobenzene reduction to phenylamine
entry.medium: strongly acidic reduction, then alkaline work-up
entry.observation: tin dissolves during reduction; no single final colour observation is required
entry.notes: NaOH liberates free phenylamine from the phenylammonium salt.

entry.title: Phenylamine + bromine water
entry.observation: bromine water decolourises and a **white precipitate** forms
entry.notes: activated aromatic ring; no AlBr₃ catalyst.

entry.title: Amide alkaline hydrolysis
entry.observation: ammonia may be evolved from primary amides; NH₃ turns damp red litmus blue
entry.notes: acidification afterwards gives the free carboxylic acid.

entry.title: Amino acid + acid
entry.notes: basis of electrophoresis behaviour at low pH.

entry.title: Amino acid + base
entry.notes: basis of electrophoresis behaviour at high pH.

entry.title: Polyester from diol + dicarboxylic acid
entry.observation: viscous polymer forms; water is eliminated
entry.notes: exact laboratory apparatus/temperature is not normally memorised.

entry.title: Polyester from diol + dioyl chloride
entry.reagent: monomers themselves; base may be used to remove HCl
entry.observation: polymer may form rapidly at interface
entry.notes: acyl chlorides are more reactive than dicarboxylic acids.

entry.title: Polyester from hydroxycarboxylic acid
entry.observation: polymer formation; no distinctive colour change
entry.notes: one monomer contains both functional groups.

entry.title: Polyamide from diamine + dioyl chloride
entry.observation: polymer fibre/film can form at the interface ("nylon-rope" style experiment)

entry.title: Polyamide / polypeptide from aminocarboxylic acid or amino acid
Al³⁺ + NaOH
entry.products: Al(OH)₃(s), then soluble aluminate complex in excess OH⁻

entry.title: NH₄⁺ + NaOH
entry.observation: ammonia evolved; damp red litmus turns blue

entry.title: Ca²⁺ + NaOH
entry.observation: white ppt unless `[Ca²⁺]` is very low

entry.title: Cr³⁺ + NaOH
entry.observation: grey-green ppt; **soluble in excess giving dark-green solution**

entry.title: Fe²⁺ + NaOH
entry.products: Fe(OH)₂(s), then oxidation products on standing in air
entry.observation: **green ppt turning brown on contact with air**; insoluble in excess
entry.notes: air oxidation is an important observation.

entry.title: Fe²⁺ + NH₃
entry.observation: green ppt turning brown in air; insoluble in excess

entry.title: Mn²⁺ + NaOH
entry.products: Mn(OH)₂(s), then oxidised manganese species in air
entry.observation: **off-white ppt rapidly turning brown on contact with air**; insoluble in excess

entry.title: Mn²⁺ + NH₃
entry.observation: off-white ppt rapidly turning brown in air; insoluble in excess

entry.title: Bromide + Ag⁺
entry.observation: **cream / off-white ppt**, partially soluble in NH₃(aq)

entry.title: Sulfate + Ba²⁺
entry.observation: **white ppt**, insoluble in excess dilute strong acids
entry.notes: high `[Ca²⁺]` can also give white CaSO₄ ppt.

entry.title: Sulfite + Ba²⁺ then acid
entry.observation: white ppt forms then **dissolves in dilute strong acid**

entry.title: Thiosulfate + acid
entry.observation: **off-white / pale-yellow precipitate slowly forms**; mixture becomes cloudy
entry.notes: sulfur precipitate can obscure a mark beneath the flask in rate experiments. ---

entry.title: CO₂ test
entry.notes: excess CO₂ can redissolve precipitate by forming soluble hydrogencarbonate, though not required for the basic test.

entry.section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work

entry.section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work

entry.title: Alkene + HX
entry.notes: Markovnikov outcome may matter for unsymmetrical alkenes.

entry.title: Alkene oxidative cleavage
entry.products: carbonyl compounds / carboxylic acids / CO₂ depending on substitution

entry.title: Halogenoalkane → nitrile
entry.notes: carbon chain length increases by one carbon.

entry.title: Halogenoalkane → amine
entry.notes: **heated under pressure**; excess NH₃ favours primary amine.

entry.title: Halogenoalkane elimination
entry.notes: contrast `NaOH(aq)` substitution vs `NaOH in ethanol` elimination.

entry.notes: rate indicates relative C–X bond reactivity. ---

entry.title: Primary alcohol → aldehyde
entry.observation: dichromate orange → green / permanganate purple → colourless
entry.notes: **distil product as it forms** to prevent further oxidation.

entry.title: Primary alcohol → carboxylic acid
entry.reagent: excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or acidified KMnO₄

entry.title: Alcohol dehydration
entry.reagent: conc. H₂SO₄ or heated Al₂O₃ catalyst

entry.observation: often fruity ester smell, but odour should not be relied on as an exam observation unless instructed

entry.title: Aldehyde / ketone reduction
entry.medium: NaBH₄ often aqueous/alcoholic; LiAlH₄ dry ether
entry.products: primary alcohol from aldehyde / secondary alcohol from ketone

entry.notes: nucleophilic addition; introduces one extra carbon. ---

entry.reagent: dilute NaOH(aq), then acidify if free acid required

entry.title: Carboxylic acid reduction
entry.notes: strong reducing agent required. --- 1. **Benzene + Br₂:** `Br₂ + AlBr₃`, no bromine water test conditions. 2. **Phenol + Br₂(aq):** RT, no catalyst → bromine water decolourises + **white ppt**. 3. **Phenylamine + Br₂(aq):** RT, no catalyst → bromine water decolourises + **white ppt**. 4. **Benzene nitration:** conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄, **25–60 °C**. 5. **Phenol nitration:** **dilute HNO₃(aq), RT**. 6. **Diazotisation:** `NaNO₂ + dilute acid`, **below 10 °C**. 7. **Diazonium → phenol:** **warm with water**, N₂ effervescence. 8. **Alkylbenzene → benzoic acid:** **hot alkaline KMnO₄, then dilute acid**. 9. **Acyl chloride reactions:** generally **RT**; no Fischer esterification catalyst required. 10. **RX → alcohol:** `NaOH(aq) + heat`. 11. **RX → alkene:** `NaOH in ethanol + heat`. 12. **RX → nitrile:** `KCN in ethanol + heat`. 13. **RX → amine:** `NH₃ in ethanol + heat under pressure`. 14. **Primary alcohol → aldehyde:** oxidise and **distil**. 15. **Primary alcohol → acid:** oxidise under **reflux**. 16. **Methanoic acid:** positive Tollens / Fehling and decolourises acidified KMnO₄. 17. **Ethanedioic acid + KMnO₄:** must be **warm and acidic**. 18. **Cu²⁺ + excess NH₃:** deep-blue solution. 19. **Co²⁺ + excess Cl⁻:** pink → blue. 20. **Cu²⁺ + I⁻:** white CuI ppt + brown iodine. --- For implementation, each record can map directly to: ```text id topic priority reactants[] reagent[] temperature medium products[] observation[] notes[] ``` For simulation logic, separate: - `required_conditions` - `catalyst` - `solvent_or_medium` - `temperature_range` - `visible_colour_before` - `visible_colour_after` - `precipitate_colour` - `gas_evolved` - `reversible` - `reaction_type` - `exam_priority` This prevents a single free-text `observation` field from becoming hard to query later. --- - Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry 9701 syllabus, examinations 2025–2027. - A Level Topics 23–37, especially Topics 26–36. - Current Cambridge qualitative-analysis notes used for 9701 practical assessment. - Paper 4 syllabus statement: A Level questions are based on A Level content, but knowledge of AS content is required.
